info.title: Resonance API
info.description: The versioned API for the native apps. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>` (the web uses its session cookie). Additive changes only within v1.

post.summary: Onboarding: create your profile (an existing one comes back unchanged, unless it has no pen name yet)
post.description: A profile without a pen name — made before onboarding asked for one — takes the one sent (reserved, `409` when taken) with the region and writing language sent, keeping the rest; it then comes back `200`. Reaching anyone (a note, a message, a resonance that rings) takes a pen name.

200.description: Already had a profile (named now, if it had no pen name)

patch.summary: Change your pen name, bio, region or writing language

get.summary: Whether a pen name is free
One shelf of your card box
Several shelves of your card box at once
get.description: Each shelf asked for comes back exactly as `/me/cards?tab=` answers it; shelves not asked for are absent.

parameters.name: shelves
parameters.description: Shelves, comma-separated (e.g. `published,private,draft`): published, private, draft, resonated, linked, bookmarks. Unknown names are ignored.

get.summary: Latest public cards, newest first (named cards of people you blocked are left out)
get.description: Anonymous cards come without a byline, and a block never leaves one out: that would name its author.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: A page's `nextCursor` (to the millisecond: cards sharing it can be skipped). Prefer `pageToken`.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: A page's `nextPageToken`: resumes exactly after its last card. Wins over `cursor`.

get.summary: Today's picks for you, each with the reason it was picked
get.description: Answers at once from the latest picks. While today's are being prepared `status` is `stale` (earlier picks, or a quick first pass without reasons); ask again a little later for `fresh` ones.

get.summary: Several cards at once, by slug or id, as list summaries (no story)
get.description: In the order asked, each card once; cards you may not read, named cards by someone you blocked, and unknown keys are left out. Anonymous cards come without a byline, and a block never leaves one out (nor any list or feed): that would name its author.

get.summary: A card you may read, by slug or id, with its story
get.description: With `include`, the lists its page shows come along — each exactly what its own endpoint answers (`resonances`, `related`, `links`) — and `embeds`: the cards its story embeds.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The card slug, or (older cards) its id

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Lists to bring along, comma-separated (e.g. `resonances,related,links,embeds`): resonances, related, links, embeds. Unknown names are ignored.

patch.summary: Change your card's visibility and/or anonymity (only the fields sent)
patch.description: A published resonance made public under your name — published private, connections-only or anonymous, it reached no one — reaches the original's author after the response, as publishing it so would have: you two connected (not when the original is anonymous), their bell rung — once per reader and card, whatever path rang it first; never across a block, nor without a pen name. The answer never waits on it. One made private, connections-only or anonymous is at once no longer a reason you two are connected, and the connection goes when no reason is left (see `DELETE /cards/{key}/resonances/{cardId}`); the card still answers the original (listed under it while public, without your name when anonymous). An anonymous card is public or private: a change that would leave it anonymous and for connections only is `400 invalid_request` ("An anonymous card is public or private."); a card already that way stays so until either field changes.

200.description: The card as your card box shows it

delete.summary: Delete your card, draft or published (a retry after success is 404)
delete.description: A resonance is taken back with it, as `DELETE /cards/{key}/resonances/{cardId}` takes it back. The notes left on the card go with it. The only way a published card is deleted: a client may delete its own draft straight from Firestore, never a published card.

get.summary: Public cards written in response to this one

post.summary: Make one of your published public cards a resonance of this one (connects you and rings its author, as publishing one does)
post.description: A card answers one card, and you answer a card with one of yours: `409 conflict` when the card already answers another, or another of your cards already answers this one. Asking again with the same card is `changed: false` and rings no one. An anonymous card connects no one and rings no one; an anonymous original rings its author but connects no one (that bell carries `payload.anonymous`: its push opens the card). A block either way is `403 blocked` for a named original; an anonymous one is answered all the same, and the block keeps it from reaching anyone. A card public under your name needs your pen name (`403 forbidden`). While it stands it is a reason you two are connected (one more, when you already are), and the original's author writing to you while it stands (a message, or a note in your thread) answers it: a reason for good. A letter waiting between you is left as it is — only its recipient answers it.

delete.summary: Your card stops answering this one and stays as a card of its own (204 whether or not it still did)
delete.description: It no longer keeps you connected with the card's author: the connection goes exactly when no reason is left — no other resonance between you either way, no answer to one from its original's author (their message or note in your thread while it stood; words from before it never answer it, and its writer's own answer nothing), no answered letter, no accepted invite, not made before reasons were kept. A letter waiting between you is left as it was. Their bell stays too: answering that card again rings and connects no one.

204.description: It no longer answers this card

get.summary: A few recent cards sharing its tags

post.summary: Publish your card: stamps it once, gives it its slug, and lets a resonance reach its original
post.description: A resonance published public under your name reaches the original's author, the first time only: you two connected (not when the original is anonymous) and their bell rung — once per reader and card, whatever path rang it first; never across a block, nor without a pen name. A private, connections-only or anonymous one reaches no one. Either way the card is published: reaching out never fails it. An anonymous card is public or private: a draft set to be anonymous and for connections only is `400 invalid_request` ("An anonymous card is public or private.") and stays a draft.

post.summary: Apply your pending edit (cards/{id}/edits/current) to your published card, and clear it
post.description: An edit that makes a published resonance public under your name reaches the original's author after the response, as a PATCH doing so would (see updateCard); one that leaves it private, connections-only or anonymous takes it back, as that PATCH would. An edit that would leave the card anonymous and for connections only is `400 invalid_request` ("An anonymous card is public or private."), the card and the edit left as they were — unless the card already is so and the edit keeps both.

post.summary: Report a card you can see (its author, anonymous or not, is filled in by the server)

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The card slug, or its id

post.summary: Report a person or a message sent to you (the server keeps a copy of what was reported)

get.summary: Cards linking to it (empty unless you wrote it)
A person's profile as you see it
get.description: With `include`, what `/cards` (its first page, of `limit` cards) and `/links` answer come along.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Lists to bring along, comma-separated (e.g. `cards,links`): cards, links. Unknown names are ignored.

get.summary: Their public cards, newest first (never anonymous ones)

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: A page's `nextCursor` (to the millisecond: cards sharing it can be skipped). Prefer `pageToken`.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: A page's `nextPageToken`: resumes exactly after its last card. Wins over `cursor`.

get.summary: Cards by others that link to theirs

post.summary: Accept a legacy invite sent to you: connects you two and rings its sender's bell (accepting again changes nothing); it answers a letter waiting between you
post.description: `409 conflict` once it is no longer open: declined, withdrawn, or past its `expiresAt` (it is closed as `expired` then, so inboxes should list only invites before their date). `403 forbidden` without a pen name; `403 blocked` across a block either way.

post.summary: Send a note to a card's author: rings them and lands in your conversation as a message (`kind: 'note'`, `cardRef` = the card). A note is a letter: it connects no one. Between two people not connected it waits in the conversation (`request: { from, cardId, at, count }`) until the author answers it with a message, which connects you (so does a note of theirs to you while yours waits); at most 3 unanswered in all, then 409 `conflict` ("Wait for them to reply."). Either of you may delete the conversation: the writer withdraws the letter, the author declines it, and it can no longer be answered — but the count of 3 is kept apart and goes only when it is answered. Only its recipient answers it: connected some other way (a resonance), it still waits, and the recipient's message or note clears it. On an anonymous card: the bell only (`payload.anonymous` true: its push opens the card — `data.route` `/card/{cardId}`, no `fromUserId` — and a bell list should open the card too, never a thread with the writer) — no conversation, no connection; across a block it is answered 201 all the same and delivered to no one (a refusal would name its author)
post.description: A `clientId` makes sending retry-safe: it becomes the note's id (and its message's in the thread), and the same one sent again (a retry after a lost answer) is answered `201` with that id as it was first sent, writing, counting and ringing nothing, while the note is there — whatever has become of the blocks or the card's visibility since. A card deleted takes its notes with it: a resend after that is `404`, as any note to a missing card is. Someone else's note, or a message already in the two people's thread on a named card, is `400` ("Not a valid client id.").

post.summary: Message someone you are connected with (opens the conversation; its first message rings their bell), or answer a note they left you while you weren't (`request.from` is them): that answer connects you — and answers it all the same once you are
post.description: Checked in this order: the contract (`400`); your message budget (`429`); the request itself (`400`: messaging yourself, no text and no card, a `clientId` or `replyTo` Firestore keeps for itself); `cardRef` (`404` for a card you can't read); a `clientId` already used — yours answers `201` as it was first sent, someone else's is `400`; your pen name (`403 forbidden`, "Choose a pen name first."); a block either way (`403 blocked`); the connection (`403 forbidden`, "You can message people you are connected with.", unless a letter of theirs waits in your conversation — then your answer connects you); `noteRef`, a note they left you on the card it names (else `400`, "That is not a note they left you."); `replyTo`, a message of this conversation (else `400`). A reply to a note left on your anonymous card, or to a note no longer there whose card is gone too (deleting a card deletes its notes) or isn't yours, is sent without its `noteRef`, saying nothing of the card — and still answers a letter; a note no longer there on your own card, still there, is the `400`. A message from the original's author of a resonance standing between you, to its writer, answers that resonance (see `unresonateCard`).

put.summary: Register this install's push token (it moves to you if someone else was signed in on it)

parameters.name: installationId
parameters.description: The install's own stable id (8–128 of A–Z a–z 0–9 _ . : -)

delete.summary: On sign-out: stop pushing to this install

ApiError.description: Every non-2xx response has this shape.

AccountDeletionStatus.description: A scheduled deletion of the account (what GET /api/account/deletion answers as `deletion`).

CardBox.description: Shelves of your card box, each one asked for (and only those) exactly as GET /me/cards?tab= answers it.

status.description: fresh: today's picks. stale: earlier (or quick, reason-less) picks while today's are prepared; ask again later. Absent: fresh.

RecommendedFeed.description: Today's picks (a CardList, plus whether they are today's).

image.description: A site-relative path ('/api/link-image?u=…&s=…'): resolve it against the API's origin. Null when the page had no picture.

LinkPreview.description: What a link says about itself: the title, description, site name and picture of its page, as the server read it.

linkPreviews.description: Previews of the links standing alone in the story, in reading order (at most 10). Draw such a paragraph as a link card when its normalized URL has a preview here, else as the plain link. Absent from older servers.

CreateProfileRequest.description: Onboarding: the pen name, region and writing language of a new account.

UpdateCardRequest.description: Your card's visibility and byline; only the fields sent change.

ResonateRequest.description: Make a card you have already written a resonance of this one.

SendNoteRequest.description: A note to a card's author (the server finds the author — anonymous cards too).

RegisterDeviceRequest.description: This install's push token. Register after sign-in and whenever the token or the app's language changes.

ReportCardRequest.description: Report a card — anonymous ones too: the server knows its author, the app doesn't.

CreateReportRequest.description: Report a person or a message. The server keeps a copy of what was reported, so deleting it later erases no evidence.

HandleAvailability.description: Whether a pen name is free (your own counts as free).
